Plymouth
Not too far away as the crow flies, a little further as the ship sails, is Plymouth which this year is celebrating the 350th anniversary of the sailing of the Mayflower carrying the 102 pilgrims across the Atlantic to become the Founding Fathers of the United States of America. Plymouth has much else to be proud of with its maritime history dating from Sir Francis Drake to Sir Francis Chichester but this year all attention will be focused on the Mayflower and its associations. The celebrations will be opened on May 2 (during the same week as our Conference) by the Governor of Massachusetts, Francis Sergent, and they will be televised on both sides of the Atlantic with the opening speeches relayed to the 29 Plymouths in America.

Home Planning Truths
by MARY GEORGE, MBE, Director EAW
WE are all looking forward with some trepidation to the advent of decimalisation. It is likely, however, that the effect will be short and sharp and that we shall soon get used to the changeover.

title: Lord
brief_context: Quoted on the benefits of metrication as 'spring cleaning'.
brief_extract: This has already begun and from now onwards we shall gradually have to get used to living with litres, grammes and metres instead of pints, pounds and yards. But, as Lord Ritchie-Calder, Chairman of the Metrication Board, has said: 'Going metric is much more than a change in arithmetic, important as that is. It is an opportunity for spring cleaning.' This suggests that there is a chance for us to look afresh at some of the things we have taken for granted over the years and to try to effect some improvements.
